description: A five-panel composite figure mixing one quantitative plot with four SEM micrographs of worn surfaces and wear debris. (a) plots wear rate ×10³ (mm³/Nm) (y-axis, ticks 0–0.4, step 0.05) versus aging time (h) (x-axis, 0–4) for Fe–22.33Mn–1.35C–9.87Al; legend entries are "As-homogenized" (crossed circle, plotted at 0 h and the highest symbol on the plot), open circles "500°C", open squares "550°C", filled triangles "600°C". Three printed linear fits are given: y = −0.0426x + 0.332 (R² = 0.97) for 500 °C, y = −0.0399x + 0.2804 (R² = 0.93) for 550 °C and y = −0.0374x + 0.2146 (R² = 0.99) for 600 °C; all three series fall with aging time, the 600 °C line lying lowest and the 500 °C line highest. (b) is an SEM worn surface with a 100 µm scale bar, arrows labelling "Craters", and a 10 µm inset. (c) is SEM wear debris of irregular flaky fragments, 100 µm scale bar with a 10 µm inset of a single plate. (d) is a worn surface annotated "1050°C+550°C(3h)", 50 µm bar, a dashed line circling a "Delamination" flake within a lamellar wear layer. (e) is a 2.5 µm-scale worn surface "1050°C+550°C(4h)" labelled "(Fe,Mn)₃AlC", "broken coarse κ" and "microcracking".
measured_quantities: coefficient of determination R² of linear fits

observations.observation: In panel (a) the 'As-homogenized' symbol (crossed circle) at 0 h has the highest wear rate of any datum plotted, above all three aged series.

Panel (a) prints three linear regression equations with R² values: y = −0.0426x + 0.332 (R² = 0.97), y = −0.0399x + 0.2804 (R² = 0.93) and y = −0.0374x + 0.2146 (R² = 0.99), corresponding to the 500 °C, 550 °C and 600 °C legends respectively.

In panel (a) all three aged series decrease with aging time from 1 to 3 h, and the 600 °C series (filled triangles) lies lowest at every aging time while the 500 °C series (open circles) lies highest; all slopes are negative.
Panel (b) is an SEM worn surface with a 100 µm scale bar and arrows labelling 'Craters', plus a 10 µm inset.
Panel (c) shows loose wear debris as irregular flaky/angular particles with a 100 µm scale bar and a 10 µm inset of a single cracked debris plate.
Panel (d) worn surface carries the annotation '1050°C+550°C(3h)' and a 50 µm scale bar, and a dashed outline marks a 'Delamination' flake in a lamellar wear layer.

Panel (e) carries the annotation '1050°C+550°C(4h)' with a 2.5 µm scale bar, and labels '(Fe,Mn)₃AlC', 'broken coarse κ' and 'microcracking', showing microcracks associated with a fractured coarse κ particle.
The caption states that (b) and (c) are the worn surface and wear debris of the Fe–22.33Mn–1.35C–9.87Al steel aged at 600 °C for 3 h.

The caption states that (d) and (e) show the worn surface of Fe–28Mn–1C–8.5Al quenched at 1050 °C and subsequently aged at 550 °C for 4 h; the image annotation in (d) instead reads '1050°C+550°C(3h)', so caption and pixel text disagree for panel (d).
The caption states the figure is adapted with permission from references [22,90], Copyright 2021 and 2016, Springer Nature.
The citing text attributes to Sohrabizadeh et al. [22] the function of aging time and wear rate for Fe–22.33Mn–1.35C–9.87Al (wt%) plotted in panel (a).

The citing text states that incoherent κ particles within the austenite matrix, produced by higher aging temperature and longer time, inhibited crack nucleation during the wear test, explaining the lower wear rate of the 600 °C aged steel.

The citing text states that Peng et al. [90] found the wear rate of Fe–28Mn–1C–8.5Al (wt%) deteriorated after overaging longer than 2 h at 550 °C because of coarsened κ particles around the grain boundaries, shown in Figure 8d,e.
The citing text states that in the 550 °C/4 h sample microcracks propagate along broken coarse κ particles, so overaged κ particles initiate cracking and delamination.
A rendered Chinese-language text box ('已检测到表格 / 点击 ESC 可退出到文本选择模式') overlays part of the inset in panel (b); this is a screenshot/annotation artifact and not scientific content.

subfigures.description: Scatter plot with three linear fits of wear rate ×10³ (mm³/Nm) versus aging time (h) for Fe–22.33Mn–1.35C–9.87Al. The as-homogenized crossed-circle symbol at 0 h is the highest point; 500 °C (open circles), 550 °C (open squares) and 600 °C (filled triangles) series at 1, 2 and 3 h form three descending lines with printed equations and R² values; the 600 °C line lies lowest, 500 °C highest.

SEM micrograph of a worn surface, 100 µm scale bar, with arrows labelling 'Craters' — dark elongated depressions/spalled regions aligned along the sliding direction; a 10 µm inset shows one crater at higher magnification, partly obscured by a rendered Chinese-language text-selection box ('已检测到表格 / 点击 ESC 可退出到文本选择模式'), which is a display artifact, not sample text.

SEM micrograph of loose wear debris: many irregular, angular to flaky debris particles on a dark background, 100 µm scale bar; the 10 µm inset shows a single large debris plate with surface cracks/lamellae.

SEM worn surface of the steel annotated '1050°C+550°C(3h)' in the upper-right, 50 µm scale bar; a lamellar/stratified wear layer with elongated slip/ploughing features, and a dashed yellow line outlining a delaminated flake marked 'Delamination'.

Higher-magnification SEM worn surface annotated '1050°C+550°C(4h)', 2.5 µm scale bar, with arrows labelling '(Fe,Mn)₃AlC' (κ-carbide particle), 'broken coarse κ' (fractured coarse carbide) and 'microcracking' propagating along the broken coarse κ particle.

unreadable_items: panel (b): the higher-magnification inset region is partly covered by a non-scientific Chinese text-selection box, so the crater interior detail there is obscured
caption vs panel (d): the printed annotation '1050°C+550°C(3h)' conflicts with the caption's statement of 550 °C for 4 h; neither can be reconciled from the pixels alone
panel (a): individual data-point coordinates are not printed as numbers — values were not estimated
